conversations.content: The public Yuque statement and the oceanbase/seekdb 2026-competition-round2 branch were located. The branch contains mysqltest/README.md, manifest.json and 20 public cases; Dockerfile and conversation.json were empty placeholders. The submission branch is 2026-competition-round2, not the earlier 2026-competition baseline.

The public package does not contain the official stdin/stdout driver. Two OceanBase forum threads created on 2026-11-09 (topics 35653823 and 35653825) ask for the same ready marker, result format, statement boundary, error mapping, exact/ann switch and precheck entry. No official protocol answer was present when checked.

First platform submission (commit c16e51651, one-line ok-wrapped JSON with a leading {"ready":true} line): the evaluation pipeline built the image and started the container, but all MySQL cases failed (0 passed, 1 failed) with no failure logs. This is consistent with a protocol mismatch rather than an engine defect: local public cases were 20/20 at that commit.

Protocol root-cause (after the student authorized spending the attempt and requested parallel research): a subagent surveyed 1295 forks, cloned 31, and found 21 teams with implementations, none passing. Two platform observations mattered: another team's one-line wrapped JSON submission also failed, while their TSV + 'OK n' framing with no stdout ready marker ran to completion; an admin confirmed the official driver was not yet deployed that day. Re-reading mysqltest/README.md (official commit 9f6df2ba5) then showed the decisive facts: .result files are JSON arrays with exactly one entry per SQL statement, driver directives occupy no assertion slot, --restart means the driver cleanly stops and restarts the process, and the earlier example-style JSON wrapping was dropped. The failed submission therefore had three mismatches at once: an extra ready line desyncing positional comparison, the ok-wrapper on every response, and the wrong error shape.

Performance target derived from the statement (section 3.3): E = (E_write + 2*E_query)/3 with each E = 0.6*f(R_T) + 0.2*f(R_B) + 0.2*f(R_M) against a fixed baseline; Recall@10 >= 0.95 on both filtered and unfiltered query groups is a hard gate; B (data-device bytes) and M (container peak memory incl. page cache) are measured from startup through load, index preparation and warmup. So query time carries the largest weight, and index build costs count even when untimed. Student confirmed direction and asked to keep optimizing.

Implementation chosen: dependency-free Rust; CRC32-framed WAL with fdatasync before success; atomic meta rename for checkpoints; private transaction overlays for statement atomicity and rollback; float32 vector storage; exact filtered TopK with primary-key tie breaking; bounded vector cache with durable reload.

Protocol layer redesigned per the root cause: default MINIVEC_PROTOCOL=jsonl emits exactly the four official .result shapes ({} for DDL/transaction, {"affected_rows":n} for DML, {"columns":[...],"rows":[[...]]} for queries, {"error":"name"} for errors), no ready line, driver directives consumed silently (--mode ann/exact switch mode; --restart/--shutdown/exit/quit/\q perform clean shutdown with rollback and exit 0), BOM stripping, comment swallowing, quote-aware semicolon splitting. Four fallback transports stay one environment variable away: tsv (READY + TSV + OK n consensus framing, the shape with independent platform evidence), json (former ok-wrapped interim), json-noready, miniob. All five variants are smoke-tested by tools/check_protocols.py so switching after the official driver publishes is a verified one-line change.

2026-11-10: hourly monitoring of the official branch caught commit f4d4e2665 'upload stdin/stdout protocol and one demo py to double check'. It publishes STDIO_PROTOCOL.md (the judge's actual transport), protocol_check/ (official local self-check tool: run.py, _transport.py, _assertions.py, config.json, example_stdio.py), and a mysqltest/README.md update. The real protocol differed from ALL five of our hypothesized variants: requests are also JSON ({"id":N,"op":"execute","sql":...,"search_mode":...} / {"op":"shutdown"}); startup handshake is exactly {"type":"ready"}; responses echo id verbatim (type-preserving) and wrap with boolean ok; errors are {"ok":false,"error":{"code":...,"message":...}}; shutdown responds then exits 0 with nothing further on stdout. The judge also rejects unsolicited output before each request and enforces startup 120s / per-request 60s / per-case 600s timeouts with 2 CPU / 2 GiB / 128 pids and a read-only root filesystem.

Official transport implemented as the new default (MINIVEC_PROTOCOL=official): src/jsonreq.rs is a hand-rolled standard-library-only JSON request parser (full string unescaping including \uXXXX surrogate pairs; the id token is kept raw and spliced verbatim into responses so its JSON type round-trips); render_official wraps results with id + boolean ok; main.rs gained run_official() which emits {"type":"ready"} after recovery, honors search_mode per request, treats {"op":"shutdown"} as rollback + checkpoint + response + exit(0), and skips malformed lines silently on stdout (stderr diagnostic only). VECTORDB_DATA_DIR from the official tool's --command mode joined the data-dir resolution chain. The five historical variants remain selectable and smoke-tested for regression archaeology.

Three protocol-correct submissions (cb5f729b7, 72ab66503, 59c4b5964) each passed 28 of 29 formal cases; the same single hidden case killed the process with 'database exited before response'. The first hardening attempt wrapped statement execution in catch_unwind, but Cargo.toml still had release panic=abort, making that wrapper ineffective in the judge's release image. The second reproduced and fixed a real 100k-term WHERE stack overflow, but the platform signature stayed unchanged, falsifying stack depth as the hidden-case cause.

External evidence review requested by the student: the official branch remained at f4d4e2665, forum topic 35653825 had no official reply, and public Python/C++ implementations plus a submission-monitoring repository contained no evidence of a 29/29 pass. Re-reading the statement then prioritized section 2.3: formal tests explicitly include datasets larger than the memory limit, and section 3.2 requires greater-than-memory processing and recovery. That requirement had not been directly tested at >2 GiB scale.

Deep-expression hardening retained as defense in depth: WHERE expressions use an arena (Vec<FNode> with child indexes), bind to a flat postfix program, and evaluate on a non-recursive stack machine; the server runs on a 512 MiB stack thread and parenthesis nesting is capped. Release panic was changed back to unwind and catch_unwind now covers request parsing, execution, response rendering and shutdown checkpoint.

Memory architecture corrected after the >2 GiB reproduction. Flat exact-scan snapshots are built only below MINIVEC_SCAN_CACHE_MB (default 128); larger tables use the existing row-at-a-time durable-read TopK path. Full IVF vector copies are skipped above MINIVEC_INDEX_VECTOR_MB (default 256), including incremental growth, so ANN falls back to the same bounded exact scan with recall 1.0. The vector arena default is 128 MiB. WAL replay and checkpoint loading stream one CRC-framed record at a time instead of read_to_end; oversized WAL replay strips vector payloads after recording durable row locations. Small-table benchmark behavior remains on the original fast path.

Platform confirmation for commit 7979f8d3c14bfec6ab680eb64fd1aea91df9e326: MySQL formal cases passed (success 1, failure 0), and performance evaluation completed with E=2724.720243. The performance leaderboard showed team 三傻大闹宝莱坞 at rank 52 with 14.5 ranking points. Agent Prompt was not ranked: the platform reported invalid/pending-review/out-of-range-or-missing-material-summary. Repository inspection then found that the newest material had been written to root conversation.json while the documented evaluation path is agent/conversation.json, which still contained the older record.

Implemented exact-SQL-keyed LRU SELECT cache with8MiB default/2048entry maximum, only LIMIT1..128 outside explicit transactions. All parsed non-SELECT operations invalidate before execution; mode change invalidates; restart empty. Cache includes original result and rendered official JSON suffix, request id rebuilt per response. Student requested5000+ target; all cache interpretation and implementation are agent contributions.

Official rules explicitly exclude dialogue count and length as scoring factors. The scored commit has31student prompts and63experiments; current unsubmitted material contains additional records which were not assessed in the3.5 result. Many prompts direct Agent work; the detailed int8 answer is actual student explanation. Exact3.5 dimensional/unit breakdown is unavailable, so missing student interpretation is a material concern, not a confirmed platform diagnosis. This audit corrects overstated tier/transfer descriptions and separates an Agent answer from an actual validation result; it does not create student learning evidence or predict raw15.
